data.translation: Wenn der junge Weinberg – man nennt ihn ġarzík – ausgeschlagen hat, dann pflügt man um (die Weinstöcke) herum.

rationale: First III Preterit box; l-marked vineyard is the noncausative subject.

data.turoyo: Maḥtíwayna ṣeniye dmaye aʕlayye ŭ maḥtíwayna i+šuqayo baynaṯṯe, maḥtíwaynanne baynaṯṯe, hul dyurqowa.
data.translation: We would put a serving bowl of water onto them and place that broadcloth within them, and we put it within them until it became green.

data.translation: Uncle Isho: They would put out leaves again. Yes, those trees they would just cut, like pruning a vineyard...

summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 1b in Preterit (Jan 2.31/5175)

data.turoyo: Omər: "Lo taʕibət buwwe w lo zrəʕlox, lə mawraqlox w lo mrabelox (gaḥxo), əno manfaqliloxyo w ʕayəqlox aʕle.
data.translation: He says: "You did not toil over it and you did not sow it; you did not make it leaf out and you did not raise it (laughs). I brought it out for you, and you were distressed over it.

rationale: Only source for transitive subsense 1b; coordinated personal-agent forms and plant affected theme.

summary: Both I and III denote noncausative greening. In JTM 1.1/43 the III Preterit has an overt l-marked undergoing subject; III does not imply causation here.
The lentil passage 6/52 alternates III kmawrqi with neighboring Detransitive processing forms; retain its existing filing.
The contracted morəq of 113/176 is supported by the vegetation context, but its exact phonological relation to mawrəq remains to be checked.

III is not uniformly causative: Jan has both noncausative greening subjects and a human-agent causative frame. The inherited grün werden gloss is retained for its attested meaning; 1b supplies the different valency instead of rewriting 1.
III Preterit already exists as a round-1 proposal. mawraqqe adds plural form evidence to its thin cell, while mawrəqiwo supplies the still missing III Infectum-wa.
The source shapes mawrəqiwo/mawraqqe/mawraqlox must not be normalized from translation. No new waraq-based etymology is established by the foliage noun association.
Is there a dialectal or aspectual distribution between I yarəq/yorəq and III mawraqle/mawrəq? These few passages establish overlapping meanings, not a conditioning rule.
Confirm the contracted morəq in 113/176 and feminine dyurqowa in the broadcloth passage.
Obtain native/editorial translations of all Jan quotations; the English is machine output.
Confirm the understood plant and human-agent interpretation in the Jonah speech, and whether 1b is a productive causative of greening or a narrower foliage-growth use.
Confirm the contraction in plural mawraqqe and the relation of mawrəq foliage uses to the established yrq entry; no independent loan history is asserted.
Treated cloth can become green; the clause describes the cloth's colour change, not an external agent dyeing it.

Trees putting out foliage and barley becoming green after rain support the intransitive meaning established in round 1. Plant type and regrowth are participant/aspect extensions, not additional lexical senses.
